endorsements.quote: AI is just tool to increase comfort and will always be complimentary to clinician.
AI can save time and effort of clinician by doing repetitive task, but clinicians should not blindly follow AI model but think while apply ing results in their clinical work.
Institutions and clinicians associated with ML should be responsible for the outcome.

unlisted_practices: Ensure patient privacy, informed consent, counselling, and transparency in AI modules to build trust.
Collect and share larger, standardized datasets across institutions and integrate health, laboratory, and imaging records to improve AI performance.
Train AI models on representative data from multiple regions and languages for deployment in diverse, low-resource settings such as India.
Medical personnel should remove bias when adapting AI in the medical system.
Clinicians should not be deterred from exploring further uses of AI and should embrace it, despite its limitations.
Prioritize AI safety and avoid over-reliance on AI.

screen.reason: An editorial overview discussing the potential applications, ethical considerations, and limitations of AI in obstetrics and gynaecology.
